title: Transforming Software Development with Generative AI: Empirical Insights on Collaboration and Workflow
extended_summary:
This paper examines how generative AI tools such as ChatGPT and GitHub Copilot are changing software development work practices and collaboration. The central research question is how software engineers’ individual work practices are being transformed by generative AI and what implications this may have for teamwork and collaboration in software product development.

The study uses an exploratory multi-case qualitative design based on semi-structured interviews with 13 professionals working in software-intensive organizations. Participants included data scientists, managers, developers, designers, frontend developers, architects, and technical leaders. The paper documents a range of uses for generative AI, including getting unstuck on tasks, learning new concepts, creating simulated environments, writing emails and presentations, generating boilerplate text and code, refactoring existing code, debugging, and generating tests. The authors also distinguish between simple dialogue-based use and more advanced prompt-engineering-based use.

The population is not an education sample and does not involve school, secondary, or high-school students. Instead, the context is workplace software development in Norwegian organizations connected to research programs on software development processes. Interviews suggest that participants perceived generative AI as increasing efficiency, making work more enjoyable, and boosting motivation by reducing repetitive tasks and providing rapid feedback.

The main conclusion is that generative AI is perceived as a paradigm shift in software development workflows: it can improve individual productivity, speed learning, and increase motivation, but it may also reduce person-to-person knowledge sharing and disrupt team learning loops. The paper raises concerns that relying on AI instead of colleagues could negatively affect agile teamwork and collaboration over time. Because this is a qualitative interview study with adult professionals, it is not the alleged 2026 randomized high-school ChatGPT writing trial and should be excluded from any quantitative synthesis on ChatGPT-based writing feedback in high school.
quality_tier_rationale: This is an exploratory qualitative multi-case interview study with 13 software-industry participants. It is not an education study, not randomized, and provides no quantitative causal estimates, so it meets only limited credibility criteria.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports perceived positive and mixed impacts, but effects are unclear because there are no quantitative outcome estimates or effect sizes. Impact cannot be credibly placed above unclear/modest based on the available evidence.

interventions.use_case: Generative AI tools (primarily ChatGPT and GitHub Copilot) used by software professionals for code generation, debugging, learning, drafting text, and workflow support in software development teams.

finding.finding_summary: Interviewees qualitatively reported increased motivation, enjoyment, and work satisfaction from using GenAI, especially because it reduced tedious and repetitive tasks. However, these are self-reported perceptions from 13 interview participants, with no validated motivation scale, no experimental design, and no effect size reported.
finding.measure: Qualitative interview reports about motivation, enjoyment, and work satisfaction

finding.finding_summary: Participants reported that GenAI supported learning, problem framing, and 'rubber-ducking' style reflection, but also suggested reduced pair programming and less colleague interaction, potentially weakening team learning loops and collaboration. These findings are interpretive and qualitative only, based on interview themes rather than direct performance assessment.
finding.measure: Qualitative interview reports about learning, collaboration, pair programming, and knowledge sharing

finding.finding_summary: The paper's strongest empirical claim is that interviewees perceived GenAI as improving efficiency and productivity by accelerating coding, drafting, testing, and other repetitive tasks. Evidence is anecdotal and qualitative (e.g., one manager reported reducing bid-writing time to about 20 minutes), with no controlled comparison, standardized productivity measure, or effect size.
finding.measure: Qualitative interview reports of perceived productivity, efficiency, and time savings

finding.finding_summary: The study suggests GenAI may alter team collaboration patterns in software organizations, reducing some coworker interactions while increasing knowledge sharing about prompt engineering. These are exploratory organizational observations from a small multi-case qualitative study, not causal institutional estimates.
finding.measure: Qualitative interview reports about teamwork, collaboration patterns, and workflow change
